mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which positively impacts corporate earnings and drives up stock prices, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time over a 20-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate signals a strong labor market, which is positive for economic growth and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by 0.2pp in the last month
failure_condition: If UNRATE decreases but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time over a 5-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: When both the unemployment rate decreases and payroll employment increases, it indicates a robust labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE decreases and PAYEMS increases but S&P 500 returns are not positive more than 60% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate indicates tighter monetary policy, which can negatively impact borrowing costs and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.25pp in the last month
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS increases but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time over a 60-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates strong consumer demand and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time over a 20-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in CPI indicates higher inflation, which can lead to decreased consumer purchasing power and negative impacts on corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by 0.5pp in the last month
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL increases but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time over a 5-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is high and CPI is low, it indicates a potential mismatch in monetary policy and inflation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days as markets adjust.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is high and CPIAUCSL is low but S&P 500 returns are not positive more than 60% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in industrial production growth indicates potential supply chain issues or reduced economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth rate decreases by 1pp in the last month
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth slows but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time over a 60-day horizon.
